lines.text: Every winter, my grandfather fished the same frozen lake, from the same little shack, over the same hole.
He had one rule. If something knocks from under the ice... you never knock back.
This was my first winter out there alone. Just me, a lantern, and a hole drilled through two feet of ice.
Around midnight, my line went slack. Then, right under my boots...
I stepped back toward the door. The knocking followed me. Step for step.
I told myself it was the ice settling. Lakes crack and groan all winter.
Then I looked down into the fishing hole.
A face was pressed up under the water. Pale. Eyes open. Smiling.
It was my grandfather. He went through the ice eleven winters ago. We never found him.
His knuckles rapped the underside of the ice, right beside my boot. Knock. Knock.
And my hand... my own hand... knocked back.
The ice around the shack split, in a perfect circle. And the cold pulled me down.
So if you're ever out on the ice, and something knocks from below... don't knock back. It's probably me.
